name: Puwa Yi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Retired Glottolog entry; Puwa Yi [ypw] split in 2008 into Hlepho Phowa [yhl], Labo Phowa [ypb], Ani Phowa [ypn]; no description of this languoid as such located

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid and reference records for phow1235, hlep1236, labo1243, anip1235, high1272 (langdoc tables, 25-32 refs).
sources.note: Bibliography only; no grammar exists for any Phowa variety; only phonology-tagged items are Pelkey 2008 (thesis), Wang 2003, and Fried 2000 (Phukha [phh], outside ypw scope).
No phonology content; cites only Ethnologue.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority 2007. Change Request 2007-122 (submitted by Jamin R. Pelkey): split [ypw] Puwa Yi into [yhl] Hlepho Phowa, [ypn] Ani Phowa, [ypb] Labo Phowa (adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; establishes identity only: ypw = Phowa dialect continuum whose three extremes (Ani, Labo, Hlepho) are mutually unintelligible.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: toward the synthesis and statement of a sub-branch. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 6.1 'Ani Phowa' (pp. 58-60, scanned; PDF has no text layer): 42 consonant initials, 11 vowels, 'Phowa utilizes five tonal contrasts: high, mid, low, low-rising, and low-falling' plus a tense-lax phonation contrast; no statement about stress/accent anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent full scanned: 'stress' only in non-phonological senses).
